utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you may have noticed on the other photo-boards that same person is -- has a far less blue background than he has on this version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm very well aware of that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, after you had the photo-board compiled and sent back to you from mapping, did you have an opportunity to show the photo-boards -- the three photo-boards to somebody on your team or somebody else who did not know who Idriz Balaj was so you could determine whether or not it was a good photo-spread in your estimation?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: At that stage, we didn't know if Mr. Balaj was the right person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: And if I can continue, I mean, it's a landscape office and everyone in the team reviewed these photo-boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Now, with regard to your particular practice in showing individuals photo-boards of which you showed a number of people photo-boards, did you, once receiving an identification, whether it be positive or negative, use the same photo-board again or did you change the photo-boards that you used?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I mean, we had three different sets of these photo-boards, and we were picking out a photo-board in random, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. So what that would mean -- and the reason you had three different sets of photo-boards was because of what precisely, why three sets?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Because not to use one single one to show every -- each witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And is that because it's an important thing when you're showing photo-boards to put the individual in a different position when you're showing a photo-board board to multiple witnesses because of the possibility that somebody might talk to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, that's one of the -- one of the rules that exists and the policy, which is once you have -- it says a positive identification, I've expanded it to a negative identification, too, that ideally the photo-board should be used with other witnesses; however, if this is necessary, the positions of the photograph should be changed and the suspected's photograph in particular should be moved; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we had only these three sets of photo-boards and we were using them with all our witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I'm concerned with what you were doing, sir, not with what anybody else was doing at the moment. With regard to what you did when you showed witnesses photo-spreads specifically regarding Mr. Balaj, you took care in this regard to make sure that his position changed from witness to witness, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I hope I did. I can't say now for sure. I might have shown some witnesses the same -- the same number -- let's say the same photo-board.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you might have, do you have any records that would indicate what you did in this regard? And by that I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- personal record that shows which photo-board you used with regard to each witness?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we -- we marked the photo-boards with let's say A1 or annex 1 or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, as I say, hope springs eternal. Would it surprise you, sir, if I told you that each and every photo-board you showed to witnesses concerning my client, Mr. Balaj, he was in position number 6?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You don't believe that that in any sense affects the effectiveness of the photo-spreads -- excuse me, the photo-boards that you were showing; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. I'd like to go to the -- another aspect of the compilation of the photo-boards, which is when you were compiling the photo-boards themselves, did you attempt to make sure that the individuals who were in the photo-boards were the same or of similar ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I believe they were, because we picked them out from the applications.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you believe that they were, your basis of belief is that you picked all of the potential foils from the same group of photographs, and by that I mean body of information, which is the applications as you put it, so you made an assumption that they were all the same ethnic background. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I never searched, I mean, the backgrounds of the other persons. I just picked the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before you showed any individual a photo-board, and specifically the individuals who you have mentioned in your statement, would you agree with me that you did not obtain a physical description from any of them? And by "physical description," I mean the height, the weight, the hair colour, any distinguishing marks --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You did not. With regard to each of the witnesses who you showed photo-boards to, I take it that you attempted to make a determination of whether or not any of those witnesses were familiar with the faces - and specifically the face of Mr. Balaj - before you showed him or her any photo-boards? And by that I mean you made a determination of whether or not they had seen him on television or in the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: In the beginning when we used these first photo-boards, it was more to get convinced ourselves that those persons who pointed out Mr. Balaj as a potential perpetrator, we made this photo-board to show those witnesses and ask them if they can recognise Mr. Balaj they have been speaking of from these photo-boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I -- okay. I take it then your answer to my question would be, no, you did not make a determination whether they had seen him on television; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You were aware, of course, that Mr. Balaj was in trial in the year 2002, and specifically in trial in a relatively, shall we say, notorious trial, called the Dukagjin trial, were you not?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Later on I became aware of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say later on you became aware of it, that was sometime before you started showing these people photo-boards for the purposes that you've described to us?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I don't know the dates when I became aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you personally check to see how often his likeness had been shown on television --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- in 2002? Did you personally check to see how often his likeness had been shown in a newspaper in 2002?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ask any of your colleagues whether or not they had done that so you could have that information from them?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is the photo-board that you compiled a photo-board that you sent to a member of your team to use for an interview? And by that I mean Mr. Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, everyone in the team knew about the photo-board and it was decided to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And were you involved in sending that photo-board to Mr. Raatikainen in 2002 for interviews?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: What do you mean here by sending it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you supply it to him? Did you give it to him?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, of course, he was my team leader sitting in the same office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After you compiled it and had put it together, my question to you is: Was he -- did he ask you to use it -- he ask to use it so that he could go out and do an interview in 2002?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I can't tell you if he was using those boards, but it was clear to me that we are going to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. And the photo-boards that we are referring to are the ones that you've testified to, that you've seen up on the screen, those three photo-boards; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've told us that you did not complete the photo-board identification procedure report that is contained in the ICTY guide-lines because - and I - if I understood your evidence correctly, because the outcome would be the same. I think that's at page 35.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right? Okay. Now, with regard to the photo-board identification procedure report, there are a series of -- there are a series of -- there are a series of questions and responses that the investigators to engage in so that there is a record of what actually happened during the photo-board showing; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And among other things, one of the things that you were supposed to do is to record the witness's reactions; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's a question.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the reactions that you were to record, I take it you understand this from your previous experience of some number of years in serious crimes, is not only a verbal reaction but any kind of physical reaction that a potential witness might have; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I would -- I would put it in the statement, the reactions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: If there are any reactions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if there are no reactions, that's something -- that's something also that could be of importance; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is not information that's contained in any of the statements -- in any of your recordations of what occurred during the photo-board procedure, is it, physical reactions?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I guess no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just as important as a positive identification for your purposes would be a negative identification; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, if you received a negative response, you were to follow the exact same procedure as you were if you received a positive response, which is that you'd have the witness sign at some place that particular photo-board so that you have an accurate record of what the witness viewed; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Just a moment. I will read your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in this case, when you received a negative response, as I believe you did on a couple of occasions, did you memorialise that by having the witness sign the back of that particular photo-board so there would be a record for this Chamber to view when there had been a non-identification?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm sure. It says in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's not my question. Did you have the witness sign the photo-board in the same way that you would have the witness sign or mark the photo-board where there was a positive identification? When you received a negative one, did you have him do that?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I believe I did it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. During the time that you were showing the witnesses photo-boards, if I understand your evidence correctly, you were in the room, an interpreter was in the room, and the witness was in the room; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us, if you recall, where you would place yourself with the witness while you were showing the witness the photo-spread -- I'm sorry, the photo-board, to maintain consistency?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: In the same normal order as we were sitting during -- or when I took the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would be -- you would be across from the person, would you not?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, after you first obtained the picture of Idriz Balaj from the application forms, you knew that that was the individual, by that I mean you knew that was the individual who was the focus of your investigation; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: We knew that the name was Idriz Balaj, but we were not convinced at that stage that we had the right person, as I told you already earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. In terms of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I seek some clarification there. Witness, you say that you did not know the individual who was the focus of your investigation. Now, you are choosing eight photographs, of which you know one is of a person by the name exactly the same as the person whose name you heard several times from witnesses. Even if you are not sure yet that this is an identical person with the person mentioned by the witnesses, where you did not pay any attention to the other seven who were the name -- whose -- who they were, what their names were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would you still say that you are not focusing at that -- that photograph of a person by the same name would not be the focus of your investigation at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Of course it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- the focus of our investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the question, I think, that I mean you knew that was the individual who was the focus of your investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your answer was no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I didn't. We knew the name was Idriz Balaj, but we were not convinced at that stage that we had the right person. So I take it, and you correct your answer, that that -- the photograph of that person of which you were not sure yet whether it was the person mentioned by the witnesses, but you knew it was Idriz Balaj was the focus of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss with your colleagues as you were going through the showing of photo-boards that perhaps it would be better practice for somebody who did not know the identity or the likeness of my client, Mr. Balaj, to show the witnesses these photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you make a determination with regard to the witnesses who you showed photo-boards to whether or not they had any contact with any of the other witnesses who you had shown photo-boards to?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Well, usually they were quite afraid to give statements at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that may be the case --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: So -- yeah, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- but that's not my question.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you make a determination as to whether or not there was any contact between these people?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I believe not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, you indicated a half an hour to 45 minutes earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have two more questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- and I was watching the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we now --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have two more questions, and I was watching the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I checked, and it may only be one depending on the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which is: Did you, sir, ever ask your colleague Mr. Quiroz to forward to the mapping unit the photo-board that you compiled?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I can't remember telling him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you can't remember telling him that - and I do apologise, it's three questions now - Mr. Quiroz came on board sometime I believe in 2003; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, that might be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that would have been after you'd --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- already compiled -- that would have been after you'd compiled the photo-board and sent it to mapping unit, right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't know whether or not, and I think it's of perhaps some importance. I know this is an exhibit now, but I would like to have these three photo-boards made somehow or other separately identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you mentioned for the first the ERN number, and then you spoke about it the two following these ones. If you would check, I would do that as well, whether they are --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the subsequent numbers, ERN numbers --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, I don't think that there's any need to exhibit them separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fine. They are sequential, 7619, 7620, and 7621.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, last four digits of the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, are you ready to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I am. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey is counsel for Mr. Brahimaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Haverinen.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Before we get started I'm going to be asking you a number of specific questions in relation to your actual practices when you interviewed one particular witness and I want to make sure that you know who we're talking about when I refer to particular witness numbers that we are using for the protection of witnesses' identities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So perhaps if we can go into private session for a moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Just so that I can give you the names and then you can perhaps make a note of them so that you'll have that available to you to avoid any confusion while I'm asking you questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we turn to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Haverinen, you interviewed Witness 6 in the Pristina field office on the 25th of February of 2004, and subsequently you had a follow-up interview with him at his home on the 2nd of March, 2004. Do you recall that or do you need -- I see you turning to your 92 ter statement. Do you wish to just refer to that note to confirm that, sir? Do you wish to --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah - no- I'm sure it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And then immediately after that second interview which was on the 2nd of March of 2004, you, I take it, returned to Pristina and with one day intervening, on the 4th of March, 2004, you interviewed Witness 30. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I note, for the record, that you are looking at your statement in order to confirm those dates.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could put the statement to one side now as we continue. Your initial interview of Witness 6 you have said that you had to do a follow-up interview with him because you hadn't had time to write up your notes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In what form did you take your notes during that first interview with him?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I believe I made notes in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So not on a computer?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Not on a computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And was that in a notebook or on loose sheets of paper?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It's a notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And during the course of that first interview -- first of all, to the best of your recollection, if you're able to assist us, how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Excuse me, which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: How -- the first interview in Pristina with Witness 6 on the 25th of February, 2004.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I have no clue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: During the course of that first interview in Pristina, that took place in the field office; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, I know I have interviewed him in the field office in Pristina, but I have also met him at his house several times, so I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Going back to the field office where that first interview is recorded as having taken place, you had access there to photo-boards; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you show him photo-boards during that first interview?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I will recall that I showed the photo-boards to him in his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, the whole purpose of these two interviews was to show him photo-boards, was it not?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Are you saying that you didn't show him photo-boards in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Well, now -- now I'm thinking that yes, of course, I have showed him photo-boards in Pristina. It must be like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I appreciate this is some time ago. Do you also recall that you showed him a number of individual photographs, not -- aside from the photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: First of all, what happened to your notebook, where is that now, in which you recorded your initial interview with Witness 6?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It might be back home, in Finland.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I would be grateful if you would please check to see if it is, and perhaps you could notify Mr. Re to let us know if it is there.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. The photo-board which is annex number 5, line-up number 4, which shows my client, Mr. Brahimaj, do you recall -- did you compile that photo-board yourself?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Who did compile it, if you know?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I believe it was Jose Quiroz.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you know of your own knowledge where the photograph of Mr. Brahimaj came from for that photo-board?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Secondly in relation to the compilation of photo-boards, did you compile annex 8, line-up number 7, which contains the photograph of Witness 37? And if you need to look at your statement --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I don't. I know what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: And I have -- I can't recall doing it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Does that mean that you don't think you did it, or you don't know one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I don't think I did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you have any idea who did?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And again as to the photograph that appears as number 2 on that photo-board of witness - which is said to be Witness 37 in this case - do you know where that photograph came from?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Could you just explain, please, what was your reason for showing photographs of individual victims to Witness 6?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Why I showed him photo-boards?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, not photo-boards. Individual --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Individual --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- photographs.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we had individual photographs of persons allegedly abducted by the KLA or missing persons and also allegedly taken to Jablanica to the prison in Jablanica. And I believe the purpose with witness number 6 was to show him those photographs in order to find out whether he could recognise any of those persons being present in the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You already had some -- two statements from Witness 6 before you took these photographs to him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you already had, I think, three statements from Witness 30 at that stage?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: That might be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you asked Witness 6 about -- and you gave him the name of Witness 30 before you actually showed him a photograph, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, that was a name that he hadn't given you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, he didn't give that name to me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And he didn't recognise the photograph either, did he?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, no, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Why did you give him the name of somebody he hadn't mentioned to you and whose photograph he didn't recognise?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Because they both told me that they had been in Jablanica at the same time in the prison, then it was quite normal to ask a witness whether he could remember another prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So, in effect, you were seeking to prompt his recollection by offering him a photograph and a name to see if that would be something that he could then adopt and put into his statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No, but it was also as important -- it was also important to get it right, that if he could not recognise this person, then it has to be also written down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, before you continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of your last questions is really puzzling me. "Why did you give him the name of somebody he hadn't mentioned to you and whose photograph he didn't recognise?" Where in one of your earlier questions you said that the name was given already before the photo was shown to him. So how could you then ask -- at least I fail to understand: "Why did you give him the name of somebody and whose photograph he didn't recognise?" When that took place only after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I realised as I was asking the question that it wasn't particularly well-formulated. The question should have simply stopped with: "Why did you give him the name of somebody that he didn't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Self-correction might have been in place here, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I was hoping to get away with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Witness, let's be more serious, though. You were trying to prompt Witness 6, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Were trying to prompt, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were trying to nudge his recollection?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: In a way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And is that something that you consider is part of the directions that you received, the guide-lines that you received, in identification procedures?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No. It was a question of reliability of a witness, for both of them we have been discussing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, that's always true in questions of identification, isn't it, whether the witness is reliable?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The question is whether you considered prompting a witness's recollection as consistent with the guide-lines that you had been given?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I might have been, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you also consider it consistent with the guide-lines to tell the witness that he got the name of a suspect wrong and to give him the suspect's actual name? And I see you shaking your head in puzzlement. I'll give you the specifics. The witness had told you about somebody called Hamz Brahimaj. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I can remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You showed him a photograph of Myftari Brahimaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: That's how we knew him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And you told the witness that that is not Hamz, that's Myftari, did you not?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I can't recall that. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Again, is that something that you consider consistent with the guide-lines?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Why did you do it?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: To get sure that he was -- to be sure - how should I say it? - that he was talking about the right person.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It's one thing to say: Do you recognise this person? Would you not accept that it's quite another thing to say: No, you've got the name wrong, that's somebody else?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I don't have my statement here, but I can hardly believe that I have said that: No, you have got something wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In fairness to you, perhaps I should read to you the relevant paragraph of Witness 6's statement, and you can respond as to whether or not you believe that that is how you conducted this particular part of the procedure. It's at paragraph 17 of the statement of Witness 6 dated the 2nd of March, 2004, where he says: "I have now been handed over a photograph of a male person marked with a number 01483203 and can state that this person is the one who caught Pal Krasniqi and this Skender Kuci and maltreated them both very badly. I have stated in my previous statement" --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I should probably have gone -- I should have gone into private session before mentioning those names. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll go into private session, although I'm not yet convinced, but I'm also looking at you, Mr. Re. Two names --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I had thought that they were both in the public domain, but I'm being nudged from my right and we're just being abundantly cautious here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: They're in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in private session now. Madam Registrar, is that correct? We are. I do not easily contradict someone who says that persons are protected, but here for the two names mentioned, that is, Pal Krasniqi and Skender Kuci, I don't think they are in any way protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we return into open session. And, Madam Registrar, the instruction is that the -- this portion of the private session should be made public.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise for the confusion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Better this way than the other way around, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: To continue, Witness, I think you have it on the screen. There's no need for me to start again from the beginning. "I have stated in my previous statement that the person who maltreated Pal and Skender after they were caught was called Hamz Brahimaj together with Lahi and Nazmi Brahimaj. I can now state that this photograph now shown to me is the same person I have learned to be Hamz Brahimaj." And in the next paragraph, number 18: "I have now been told by the investigator that the person on the picture marked with," he repeats the number, "is Myftar Brahimaj." I'll stop there. I don't think there's any need to read anymore. But you see the point? He says that you told him --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- the name.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you agree or disagree with that?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I agree that I told him the name, yes, as it's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you specific questions in relation to how you conducted your questioning of Witness 6, both in Pristina and at his home. Was he sitting or standing when he viewed the individual photos?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I can't remember that, but I suppose that we were sitting in his oda.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And in Pristina, sitting in your office?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, that's the normal way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Does it come to this, that you've already given Mr. Guy-Smith a number of answers about your normal procedures and that you have no separate recollection of exactly how those procedures went when you questioned Witness 6. If you do have separate recollection, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In that case, I'm not going to waste the Tribunal's time by asking you all over again. But I do want you to explain, if you would, please, could you look at annex 5, line-up number 4, and at photograph U0167207. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, you have told the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before it's displayed, there is a redacted and an unredacted copy because it bears the signature of a protected witness. If you display it, could you please display the redacted copy, which is exhibit -- the second one, 1489 -- 65 ter 1489, which is Exhibit Number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has received an exhibit number. It is not -- it's an MFI number because it has not been admitted into evidence and usually public redacted versions do not need to be admitted but it has an MFI number, it has received an MFI number. In evidence, of course, is the full unredacted document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just asking that that be the one that's displayed on the screen, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In paragraph 15 of your statement, your 92 ter witness statement, you indicate that you showed this photo-board to Witness 6 and that he marked the number and signed the photo-board and it was attached to his statement. Now, as Mr. Re has pointed out, the photo-board is, indeed, signed, but can you tell us how and where he marked the number.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Well, I can see the number is not marked at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes. What is your explanation for that, Mr. Haverinen?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I have no explanations for that. It's a miss --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: A mistake from me, from my side, not to be sure that the witness circled the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So it appears that he didn't mark the photo-board?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: As you can see, there is no mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps one matter of clarification -- no. It's clear to me. It was the marked copy that was supposed to be attached to the 92 ter statement and it was not. Perhaps a reason to verify, I don't know -- I don't think that Witness 6's statement is in evidence, but whether anything is attached to his statement and whether we find anything there, because that might be important for the Chamber to know whether there is such a signed photo-board. So whether just the wrong copy has been attached to the 92 ter statement or whether there is no copy at all signed by Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, that was not my point. The -- my point is that the photo-board that is attached to this witness's statement is, indeed, signed by Witness 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but not --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- but not marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean marked, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's the point and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- to the best of my knowledge and belief, there does not exist a marked board, as the witness has now conceded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that would be different, I take it that the Chamber will receive that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And in conclusion, Your Honour, I would ask -- I would repeat my request that if the witness would be kind enough when he does return to Finland to see if he can locate his original notes, I would be grateful if those could be communicated to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. That's clear, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Re, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, briefly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I promise I won't be long.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were asked by Mr. Guy-Smith about the process of compiling photo-boards containing a photograph of Idriz Balaj, but what characteristics were you looking for in the applicants to the Kosovo Protection Force or Service when you compiled the boards?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: What characters?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were the things you were looking for when you were looking for another seven individuals to put on the photo-board? Or another way of putting it: How did you make your selection?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Not by random, but I tried to select eight -- or seven photographs that would -- would be quite close to how Balaj looked or that they were dressed in the same way, not using any hats, didn't have beards, and so on. So I just picked seven similar pictures, similar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith also asked you about the fact that photograph number 6 in several boards shown to witnesses was that -- was the photograph of Idriz Balaj. How many -- do you know or do you recall how many of the witnesses who you showed that particular photo-board to, that is, the one with Idriz Balaj in position number 6, how many of those witnesses knew each other or were in a position to talk to each other about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that is a compound question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think that the witness should first focus on whether he knows whether the witnesses he had shown the photo-board with Idriz Balaj in position number 6, whether he is aware of their possibilities to have contact with each other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at least those two witnesses I mentioned earlier in the beginning of this, they knew each other for sure because I believe they were living in the same village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You therefore would say that there would be a possibility for them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That they knew each other and they were living close to each other. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At page 69 of the transcript today, a suggestion was made by Mr. Harvey that you were trying to prompt a witness in their recollection by giving Witness 6 Witness 30's name and you said: "In a way, yes." What other reasons are there, if there are any other reasons, for you to give that second witness the first witness's name?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Well, it was quite confusing because they both stated that they had been in Jablanica prison, but in their statements they didn't know anything about each other. And that's -- that was to get -- to be convinced that they didn't know each other at all, not even by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't quite understand what you're saying by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, before you continue, let me -- one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I verified with my colleagues whether they would agree with me that Mr. Harvey, while reading a portion of the statement, undermined his own suggestion that the witness corrected the name given by the witness. The only thing he did, he asked questions, the portion read shows us that the witness then recognised the photograph and said: That's the person I mentioned -- I knew under this and this name, and that only after that, the name known to the investigator as the name of that person was given to him. So the suggestion included in what Mr. Harvey said is -- has not convinced the Chamber. I don't know whether you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: If I could just clarify the point here. I think what Mr. Re is asking about is the prompting of the witness but putting to him the name of Witness 30 rather than the -- the part concerned with the Hamz versus Myftari Brahimaj issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's true, then I totally misunderstood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise for that, and thank you, Mr. Harvey, for coming to the aid of Mr. Re, who would certainly have been able to explain to me that I was totally wrong. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Haverinen --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I do apologise. We seem to be having an interpretation problem in terms of receipt of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your movement remedied it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Re, again apologies for my misunderstanding of your question. Re-reading it, I should not have made that mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Haverinen, I'm asking you about reasons apart from attempting, in a way, to prompt the witness's recollection. What other reasons would you have had or did you have, if, in fact, you had any other reasons for suggesting a name to a witness?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: What my reasons was why I told the witness the other witness's name? Is that your -- asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said that you gave Witness 6 the name of Witness 30.

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey suggested it was to prompt the witness's recollection, and you said: "In a way, yes." My question is: What other reasons, if you had any other reasons, would you have asked him about the name -- Witness 30's name?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Because I wanted to be convinced that if he knew the name of that -- of that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sort of a cross-verification or a reliability check between two witnesses?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yeah, in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And Mr. Harvey also read to you paragraphs 16 and 17 -- I'm sorry, 17 and 18 of Witness 6's statement of the 2nd of March, 2004. I won't read it to you again, but you've recorded in the statement -- I'll just read you one line. "I have now been told by the investigator that the person on the picture marked with number 01483203 is Myftar Brahimaj." Why did you record that in Witness 6's statement, the fact that you had told the witness of the real name of the person in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It was the name we knew belonged to that photograph, and just to be sure that the witness was talking about the right person because he had pointed out the person with another name. And apparently he knew these persons in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm after is why did you, Pekka Haverinen, record in the statement that you had corrected -- or told the witness the correct name? What was the purpose of you recording what you had said to the witness in that statement?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Well, I recorded it because I said it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Bench has no questions for the witness. But, Mr. Emmerson, if there's any --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise, having not asked any questions at all, there's one matter of clarification arising out of the exchange between the Bench and Mr. Re I wanted to see if I could understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if I could just ask you one or two questions, please, about an answer that you just gave to Mr. Re. This is page 78, line 9, you said in respect of Witness 6 and Witness 30: "Well, it was quite confusing because they both stated that they had been in Jablanica prison. In their statements they didn't know anything about each other." And then you said: "And that was to get -- to be convinced that they didn't know each other at all, not even by name." And Mr. Re asked you whether that was a process of cross-verification or a reliability check. Was it your concern that Witness 6 was saying that he had been at Jablanica and indeed working in the kitchen there at a time when if Witness 30 was a reliable witness he ought to have seen him there at the same time? Is that your concern?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Both ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your concern was that one of them, therefore, may be lying?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't say so. Just like normal police work and interviews, I mean, it's quite -- you would like to know, I mean, why -- why is it like that, two people being at the same spot for a long period of time don't know anything of each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it wasn't simply a question of names, because when you showed Witness 6 the photograph of Witness 30, he'd never seen him before?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: That's -- that's what I recall him telling me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And before getting to the point where you needed to check the one against the other, you had established that on the accounts they were giving you, they should both have been there at the same time in that kitchen area at the time when Pal Krasniqi and Skender Kuci escaped. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. No further questions. Then since the Bench has no questions for you, Mr. Haverinen, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- for coming and answering all the questions. I also would like to ask you to as quickly as possible report to Mr. Re whether you found your notebook in Finland; and on the assumption that you will travel back to that country, I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're excused. We'll have a break -- Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just wish to say the next witness is -- there's an outstanding application for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the next witness will be taken by Ms. Issa, assisted by Mr. Kearney and Ms. Schweiger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I think the outstanding protective measures issue, that we would further consider that also on the basis of the information the witness provides to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, we'll start after the break in private session or in this courtroom even in closed session. We will have a break until five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two matters, if I may. Just before the witness testifies, I wonder if I can register a plea for concluding his testimony at five minutes to 7.00 so that we can take stock of the timetabling issues that arise in relation to the next witness and as I understand it several witnesses that the Prosecution indicated that it may be proposing to call next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, is it you or is it Ms. Issa who's going to examine the witness? Mr. Bajcetic, you'll first be examined by Ms. Issa, who's counsel for the Prosecution. And may I just remind you that the solemn declaration you gave when you entered the courtroom of course does not only cover the matters we discussed until now but is also covering the whole of your testimony as will now follow. Ms. Issa, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, can you state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: My name is Zarko Bajcetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And your date of birth is 21 June 1953; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where were you born sir?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I was born in Guca, Lucani municipality, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And your ethnicity is, in fact, Serbian; correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you presently have an occupation?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Because I was retired on the 31st of January, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And prior to the your retirement, where did you work?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I worked in the security information agency, formerly state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on 24 May 2007 you provided a statement to the Prosecution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to review that statement in your mother tongue, Serbian?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you reviewed it for accuracy?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You've also reviewed the English translation of that statement. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Which had been read back to you; right?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, in fact, you made a couple of minor stylistic changes to -- in handwriting to the English translation, which you initialled at paragraphs 23, 32, and 81 of that statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And after you reviewed the entire statement, both the English and the Serbian version, you -- did you sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And is it true and correct what is written in those statements?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It is true and correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the witness be shown 65 ter Exhibit 1486, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar. Mr. Bajcetic, we wait until it appears on the screen. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can just go down to the signature page, please, in the Serbian version first.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, do you recognise that signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can also have a look at the signature on the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, do you see that there? Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just for the sake of completeness, if we can go to page 9, paragraph 23 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have on page 9 no paragraph 23, Ms. Issa, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if we can just go to paragraph 23. Thank you. That's at page 7. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now we see an initial there at the end of that paragraph. Are those your initials?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can we please go to paragraph 32.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We see some words there which you've initialled. Are those your initials?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And finally, if we can just go to paragraph 81, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you look at paragraph 81 the word has been changed from "RDB operative" to "technician" and there are some initials. Are those your initials?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, does that statement, Mr. Bajcetic, reflect what you would say in court today if you were asked about the same matters that are contained in the statement?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: It does reflect all I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this 92 ter statement at this point, Your Honour, as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, however, the last question was not answered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It wasn't clear. Perhaps I can re-ask that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps -- the question was whether if you -- the same questions would be put to you today, you would give the same answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Issa, you went through all of the -- at least almost all of the corrections, but for one. If you would not have touched upon one of them, then I would have accepted that, as the witness said before, that he reviewed the English text as well. But now you dealt with three out of four and you have not dealt with the one in paragraph 84. I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I just missed that one, but we can go to paragraph 84 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although it was of course already I think in the -- in your first -- I don't know -- no. You only mentioned 81. Yes, please proceed with 84.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you see there's a handwritten change in paragraph 84 from "was recorded" is changed to the word "are," and there's some initials next to that handwriting. Are those your initials?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number to be assigned to this exhibit would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P377, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before Your Honour invites submissions from the Defence as to the admission of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I have an objection which is in substance the same as an objection that I raised to the Rule 92 ter statement of the last witness and I anticipate, therefore, that the Trial Chamber's ruling will follow it. But may I indicate the paragraph numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, but I need something to write. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very briefly it's the whole of paragraphs 15 and 21, the third sentence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 15, and you said -- yes. You said the third sentence of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of paragraph 59.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sentence beginning: "I believe shots ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- yes. First the 21, third sentence. Then 59 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, sorry, I do apologise. I've misled Your Honour or maybe I spoke too quickly. The whole of paragraph 15, 1-5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The whole of paragraph 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's not what we have on the -- oh, yes, paragraphs 15 and 21, the third sentence -- I understood that wrongly. So the whole of paragraph 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the third sentence of paragraph 59, which begins: "I believe ..." Just that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And on that, we respectfully submit the witness is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When we're talking about the third sentence of 59 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The sentence beginning: "I believe the shots ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is halfway a sentence I think: "Considering the pattern of the quite symmetric spreading of these bullets, I believe that ..." So only the latter part --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. "I believe" down to the word "people."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then paragraph 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- Everything from the beginning of the second sentence: "When checking ..." Down to the end of that page, the word "prisoners."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We object to. And as regards those latter two passages, those are not passages, as the earlier two are, which fall directly within the argument raised and resolved yesterday because these are expressions of opinion by a person plainly not qualified to express an opinion and it's a different objection which we would invite the Trial Chamber to rule upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you informed Ms. Issa in advance of your objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I didn't inform her in advance, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would certainly have helped if Ms. Issa would have been aware so she could have reviewed those portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you in a position, Ms. Issa, to respond right away?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: With respect of paragraph 15 clearly that's a paragraph which indicates what the witness was there for. I'm not sure. Perhaps we should be doing this with the witness's headphones on but subject to Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has reviewed his statement in English, so taking off the earphones might not have the result you wish.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, he actually -- he -- it was read back to him so he -- I don't believe the witness can speak English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's, that's not how I understood it. Yes, because he initialled English text, but that's then I take it for translation purposes. Okay. Let's not -- could you take off your earphones for a second, Mr. Bajcetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I save Ms. Issa some time in the sense of paragraphs 15 and 21 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the objection is in substance the same objection as that which I raised yesterday and upon which the Trial Chamber gave its ruling, and so I recognised that the Trial Chamber is likely in respect of those paragraphs to give a similar ruling. Paragraphs 59 and 65 raise a different issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, one of the problems with paragraphs 15 -- for example, 15 is that even if they give the reasons why the witness investigated certain matters, that when the question is not clear the answer could be misinterpreted. So therefore, we'll exclude 15 and 21, but it does not disallow you to ask the witness what was the reason or on what information he would have led these investigations. But then it could never be misunderstood as established facts in the statement. Then for the latter two, could you -- the objection there is that it is opinion rather than facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In my submission, Your Honour, it's not merely opinion. It's based on his own personal observations, and the witness can formulate a lay opinion based on his own personal observations. In addition to that, he is an experienced police officer -- intelligence officer who is in a position to make the types of observations that he has made in paragraph 59, for example. And in my submission, that paragraph -- that sentence must be looked at contextually in its entirety. That first part of the sentence, in fact, gives it more context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I can take you to -- for example, to paragraph 65, the words --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- for interrupting, but it appears that we've lost translation again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's wait until it's back.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Back on stream, I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If I read, for example, the line: "Those bars were normally used to tie cattle to, but considering the variety of cables and ropes and the way they were tied, they must have been used to immobilise and probably torture the prisoners." Is that experience which -- or is that opinion, not an opinion based on nothing at all. A few facts, opinion that goes quite a way --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you want me to respond, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we look at it contextually with paragraph 64, the preceding paragraph, the witness clearly indicates that he received information that this compound was used by the KLA as prison camp or detention centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I think we can, if we look at the two paragraphs together we can -- he's perfectly entitled to draw that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Draw these conclusions --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're using the word "draw," so conclusions are drawn there. I think these are conclusions that --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: They're inferences that the witness, in my submission, is capable of making and the Defence can certainly cross-examine him on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber decides, Ms. Issa, to consider what we find in 59 in that half a sentence and what we find in 65 as conclusions for the -- or inferences for the Chamber to be made. Of course you're invited to lay any foundation for the Chamber to make similar conclusions as the witness has done. But 59, the line: "I believe the shots were fired to execute people ..." is not admissible. And 65, the portion started on the first line with the word "when" up to and including the last line of page 15, ending with the words "prisoners" are not admitted. In addition to the portions I just mentioned to you and the remainder is admitted, and perhaps you could prepare a -- an amended version so that we have the redactions clear. And my final question would be the cover page gives the 14th of June, 2007, as a date which is unclear to me what -- what it means in addition to -- and where the date comes from for statements signed already in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That must be an error, Your Honour, and I can certainly amend that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then therefore the Chamber will pay no attention to the date of the 14th of June on the cover page of the 92 ter statement. And if you prepare a new one, perhaps you could get some -- one without the 14th of June on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I just want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then of course you have an opportunity to put further questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I know Your Honour has ruled on paragraphs 15 and 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But I wonder if it would be possible to hear me just on those particular paragraphs so we can revisit it. If not, that's subject to Your Honour, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not fully understand. You can ask whatever questions you'd like to ask about the matters covered by paragraphs 15 and 21, so please --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In the -- perhaps you can put your earphones back on, Mr. Bajcetic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and, Ms. Issa, you will not be surprised if you ask for exactly for the same that you will meet some objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'll bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Bajcetic, in paragraph 96 of your statement, you were shown a number of photographs. You indicated that you recognised what was depicted in those photographs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd just like to tender the 65 ter Exhibit Number 1487 which are the photographs that are referred to in that paragraph as ultimately forming part of the 92 ter statement once it's amended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the 92 ter statement or would you like to have them in a separate number?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, for the a time being we can have them as a separate number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The whole series then in one separate number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be, Madam Registrar, number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P378, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To the extent that with regard to those photographs, there are some conclusions drawn. For example, ERN 4043: "I recognise a body of a person who had obviously been beaten" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but this is part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we have ruled on the admission of the statement. We have excluded certain parts. We're now dealing with the photographs as such, and therefore -- but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you would have any specific concerns there, I would expect you to in cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to deal with it. Ms. Issa -- let me just see. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bajcetic, drawing your attention to paragraph 10 of the statement, you say in that paragraph that you were sent to Djakovica on July 1st, 1998, until the 1st of October or November, 1998, to investigate terrorist activities and the structure of the KLA. Can you provide us -- can you tell us what terrorist activities you were sent there to investigate. What was the nature of the terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: PEKKA HAVERINEN
